name: Libertarian Socialism
summary: Libertarian socialism is an anti-authoritarian, anti-capitalist current that seeks workers' self-management and direct democracy, rejecting both private ownership of the means of production and state ownership. It spans anarchist currents and libertarian Marxist ones such as council communism, and favours federated, decentralised organisation from below with direct action as its method.
scope: The mainstream of the family: the social-anarchist and council-communist core (Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin, Pannekoek, Luxemburg) as presented by Daniel Guerin and Noam Chomsky. Where strands differ, answers follow that shared anti-state, anti-capitalist core; individualist and market-socialist strands, and democratic-socialist currents in the British labour movement, are noted but not followed. Many answers not stated in these sources are carried over from the anarchist profile and marked as inferred or medium.

sources.usedFor: Council communism: rejection of parliaments and state capitalism, council delegates, labour-time accounting.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Libertarian socialists generally favour universal access to care, though many prefer it run by communities and workers rather than the state; inferred from the principles.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Libertarian socialists back workers' struggles for better pay but aim to abolish the wage system and prefer direct action over legislation, so a state-set wage is not their demand; inferred from their critique of wage labour.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Social libertarian socialists reject capitalist markets as a source of exploitation, though they oppose state allocation too and the mutualist minority keeps markets among co-operatives.

public-ownership.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state ownership as bureaucratic control; Pannekoek called it state capitalism and Chomsky cites Bakunin's warning of a red bureaucracy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposed to concentrated wealth, though many would abolish rather than reform the tax system; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalists built worker organisations as a practical school for self-management, though Pannekoek was critical of union bureaucracy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Capitalist property relations are called incompatible with freedom, though personal self-ownership is upheld.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose corporations as hierarchical institutions and want them replaced by self-management; they would curb corporate power, but distrust state regulation as the remedy.

cut-welfare.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject the idea that the poor are made dependent by aid, attributing poverty to capitalism and property, and they favour solidarity and mutual aid over cuts, though they do not idealize state welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' control of production is the core economic demand, whether through cooperatives or common ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Libertarian socialists see police and state security as core instruments of domination, so expanding state surveillance for any reason is rejected.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject laws that govern individuals' private conduct, holding that law protects privilege rather than people, so they oppose prohibition of drug use by adults.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose giving the state power to censor, preferring to confront bigots and fascists through direct community action and antifascist organizing.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejection of rulers and of any concentrated authority over others is the definition of anarchism.

state-harmful.rationale: The tradition is anti-statist, but Chomsky and democratic-socialist strands see government as accountable and sometimes a needed defence against private power, so not all call it simply harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose the state's monopoly on force and have relied on armed popular self-defence and militias, as in the Spanish Revolution, while also being anti-militarist.

empower-police-military.rationale: Malatesta names the police, soldier and prison as the essential instruments of government, and libertarian socialists are anti-militarist.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose state control over consenting adults' bodies and sexuality, though classical libertarian socialists such as Goldman treated prostitution as a product of economic exploitation to be ended by social change.

decide-locally.rationale: Federalism and decentralised self-governance are central, as the article and Chomsky describe.

rehabilitation.rationale: Libertarian socialists see crime as largely produced by property and privilege and want prisons abolished; between the two options they reject punishment, though they also reject the prison itself.

traditional-family.rationale: Libertarian socialists and anarcha-feminists treat the patriarchal family as a source of authoritarian conditioning and seek its replacement by free unions between equals.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose state regulation of personal relationships and support sexual freedom and equality, so they oppose excluding same-sex couples even while criticizing state marriage itself; inferred from anarcha-feminist and queer anarchist principles.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anarcha-feminists hold that women must control their own bodies and reproduction, as in Goldman's call that women bear children only when they want them.

more-religion-public.rationale: Most libertarian socialists are atheists who see religion as a justification of earthly authority, following Bakunin's rejection of God as master; Christian anarchism is a minority strand.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all forms of domination, including racial hierarchy and colonialism, and Black and decolonizing anarchism are recognized strands; they pursue this through social struggle rather than state programs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anarcha-feminists treat gender hierarchy and 'feminine' and 'masculine' traits as products of patriarchy rather than nature, and queer anarchism extends this; inferred from these strands rather than the classical texts.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nationalism and hold that the state creates the nation, while respecting cultures and the self-determination of oppressed peoples.

gradual-change.rationale: Most favour revolutionary or prefigurative change, though some pursue reforms while keeping anti-capitalist aims.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anarchist opposition to nations and borders leads to solidarity with migrants and campaigns against deportations and border controls.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bodies like the UN are associations of states; libertarian socialists prefer federations of free associations ('world governance') to any world government.

free-trade.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose capitalist globalization, prominently in the anti-WTO protests, as serving capital rather than workers, while also opposing national protectionism.

nation-first.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject patriotism and national interest as ideology serving the ruling classes, and are internationalist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-militarist and oppose wars waged by states, which they see as serving state and capitalist interests; a few, like Kropotkin in 1914, broke with this.

open-borders.rationale: Anarchist and internationalist strands reject nation-state borders, but the article does not state it as core.

limit-growth.rationale: The most influential green anarchist current, social ecology, blames ecological destruction on capitalism's drive to grow and favours decentralized, human-scale economies; inferred, as growth limits are not a classical theme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Libertarian socialists take ecological crisis seriously and blame capitalism, but reject state action as the solution, favouring grassroots and direct action; inferred from social ecology and anti-statism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that social problems stem from hierarchy and property, which technology alone cannot fix; social ecology accepts appropriate technology while primitivists reject it.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is centralized and state-linked, at odds with anarchist decentralization and social ecology's appropriate technology; inferred rather than stated in these sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social revolution is the stated aim of most, but reformist and nonviolent strands exist and the article records the reformism debate.

experts-over-public.rationale: Libertarian socialists accept experts as advisers but deny them any power to compel; authority must rest with those affected.

central-planning.rationale: They favour decentralised, council-based coordination from below rather than a central authority, which Pannekoek treats as a new ruling class.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualists and market socialists accept worker-owned markets, while communist strands reject markets altogether.

land-value-tax.rationale: Taxation is a function of the state that libertarian socialists want abolished, and they seek common or use-based possession of land instead; geoanarchism is a separate strand. Inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose inherited concentrations of property, aiming to end private property in land and capital altogether rather than to tax it; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional income from the state conflicts with anti-statism and with communists' aim to abolish money, but some contemporary libertarian socialists support it as relief; adherents are split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Libertarian socialists are internationalist and reject state economic intervention on behalf of national capital; inferred from their anti-nationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state control of the economy, holding production should be directed by federated producers' associations.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mutualists and individualists favour small producers' possession of their means of work, while the social anarchist majority prefers collective possession and warns that individual ownership can recreate bosses and landlords.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The wage system is rejected as exploitative; Pannekoek proposes labour-time accounting in place of wages, while money abolition is held mainly by communist strands.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Libertarian socialists would abolish central banks with the state, but most reject leaving money to the market, aiming instead at mutual banks or the end of money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies uniting employers and workers contradict both anarchist anti-statism and the abolition of the employer class.

one-party-rule.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject any party ruling the state, which they see as government by a new privileged minority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anarchism rejects all forms of rule, from monarchies to republics.

democracy-best.rationale: They endorse direct and council democracy but reject parliamentary representation, so the statement as worded splits them.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct democracy is described as central, though councils work through mandated delegates rather than mass votes on all laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism and anarcho-syndicalism put power in councils elected directly by workers, as Pannekoek and Chomsky describe.

right-to-secede.rationale: Decentralist and federalist principles imply it, but this is rarely a stated demand; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that no one should dominate another; human differences must never be turned into power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Strands disagree: pacifists reject it, while Goldman and Malatesta saw it as sometimes a necessary evil.

war-builds-character.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-militarist and see war as serving states and capital.

separate-church-state.rationale: Libertarian socialists want neither state nor church authority and are strongly anti-clerical where churches hold power, so they reject any union of the two.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject laws as such and religion as a basis of authority; even Christian libertarian socialists reject state law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Social libertarian socialists reject capitalist firms as hierarchical and want defence and dispute resolution handled by free associations and arbitration; Tucker's individualist minority accepted private defence associations.

military-superiority.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-militarist and internationalist, rejecting national military power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nationalism and ethnic discrimination and aim at a world without nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Direct action and class conflict are named as the means of social revolution, though not all adopt the historical-materialist claim.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek social equality and communists distribute by need, which goes beyond equal opportunity, though they reject identical treatment of unequal individuals.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Libertarian socialists support decolonization and hold that those most affected should lead, making indigenous self-determination over their lands consistent with their principles.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Libertarian socialists condemned colonization as robbery and support colonized peoples, though reparations paid between states are not their framework; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject political union based on religion or civilization as another form of state and nationalist identity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Social libertarian socialists see solidarity as enlightened self-interest and the egoist strand embraces self-interest outright, while rejecting capitalist individualism; adherents are split on framing it as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Libertarian socialists put individual freedom from domination first and reject obligations imposed by a community, though they see individuality as developed socially.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green libertarian socialists and deep ecologists affirm nature's intrinsic value, while social ecology, the most influential current, rejects deep ecology as anti-human; split.

limit-population.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject coercive population control and many reject deep ecology's population concerns as misanthropic; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Primitivists hold this, but most libertarian socialists reject primitivism as unrealistic and blame hierarchy and capitalism rather than civilization itself.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Libertarian socialists favour decentralized, appropriate technology under community control rather than accelerating change driven by capital; inferred from social ecology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold individuals should control their own bodies free of state interference; inferred from bodily autonomy, as the issue is not addressed in core texts.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject government decision-making as such and any authority not accountable to those affected; inferred from anti-statism.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state surveillance and support privacy and security culture against state power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek a new, stateless and classless society, not the restoration of past hierarchies.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Libertarian socialists insist means must match ends, building non-hierarchical institutions now, and reject authoritarian methods even when they promise results; inferred from prefigurative politics.

direct-action.rationale: Direct action over electoral politics is named as the route to social revolution.

means-match-ends.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that the means of change should embody the free society sought, as Chomsky's emphasis on self-organisation and SEP's account of anarchist means say.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivists reject civilization, but mainstream social libertarian socialists such as Kropotkin envisage a decentralised, technologically advanced society and most reject primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kropotkin called for combining agricultural, industrial and intellectual work so no one is confined to one specialised task for life, though libertarian socialists accept that people's talents lead them to different work.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kropotkin's 'all for all' favours need, though Pannekoek's early stage ties consumption to work.

production-for-use.rationale: They aim to replace profit-driven production with democratic planning from below to meet needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Capitalism is held to rest on labour exploitation, and wage labour conflicts with producer control.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected as state power that produces a red bureaucracy, per Chomsky citing Bakunin and Pannekoek's critique of party rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Social libertarian socialists want land held in common and worked by free associations, as in the Spanish collectives, but reject forced collectivisation and allow individual farmers who work the land themselves.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-militarist and see war as serving states and capital, though they blame the state as much as capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Libertarian socialists see government as an instrument of exploitation that takes from producers, but their main critique targets property and wage labour rather than taxation as such; inferred from Malatesta.

harm-principle.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject laws that govern consenting adults' private conduct, but they deny the state any power at all, including the harm-prevention role the statement grants it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualist libertarian socialists put the individual's rights against all groups, while social libertarian socialists stress communal good and some support collective national liberation; libertarian socialists are split.

conscription.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-militarist, oppose the state's army and have long agitated against military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Libertarian socialists value free association and the right to secede and dismiss voting for representatives, though they also favour direct democracy; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose both the state and capitalist ownership, so a state owned and run like a company is doubly rejected.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social libertarian socialists hold that real freedom requires equality and the means to live, which is why they seek common ownership and distribution by need.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Chomsky's media critique points to corporate and state power, not to media and academia as a rival to elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject racial hierarchy as a form of domination and stress human equality; inferred, as they rarely address the genetic question directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject parties and would organise society through federations of communes and workers' associations, though they want mandated delegates rather than corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Anarchism seeks to abolish the state altogether.

national-rebirth.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nationalism and patriotism as ideologies of the ruling classes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Libertarian socialists are anti-imperialist and anti-militarist and reject state borders altogether.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all hierarchical authority, including personal lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all forced labour and want land free to those who work it.

universal-morality.rationale: Social libertarian socialists ground their politics in universal human dignity and Kropotkin saw mutual aid as natural to all humans, while egoists reject universal morality; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Libertarian socialists favour diversity and free association over any single blueprint imposed on society; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose all states and nationalisms, and Israeli libertarian socialists question Jewish nationalism and organise in joint struggle with Palestinians.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from scepticism of nation-state citizenship.

revive-national-language.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject a state language and deny that language reflects a special national unity, though they support oppressed cultures; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' self-management without bosses, appointed by employers or the state, is the defining demand.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed in the source; inferred from anarchist opposition to both the state and capitalism, which makes state-funded private school markets unattractive, while many libertarian socialists also favour free, self-managed schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed in the source; inferred that libertarian socialists reject the state's management of the economy, so neither deficit stimulus nor fiscal discipline is an anarchist position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian socialists see capitalist property and wage labour as forms of domination that undermine freedom, so for them political freedom requires ending, not protecting, market economic 'freedom'.

rule-by-example.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject rule itself and hold that authority corrupts rulers as well as the ruled, so they would not rely on rulers' example; they also reject laws and punishments, so the rejection of the statement is partial.

national-self-determination.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject the nation-state and say the state creates the nation, but they back the liberation of oppressed peoples, so they deny a right to a state while supporting self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose states, armies and militarism and reject wars waged by governments, whether or not an international body approves them.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Most libertarian socialists are atheists who follow Bakunin in rejecting divine authority and appeal to science and reason, but religious libertarian socialists exist and emotion and solidarity matter, so the agreement is not total.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nations and borders and hold that people living and working somewhere share equally in common resources, so citizenship-based limits on benefits contradict their internationalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state-imposed conditions and want needs met by free association and distribution according to need, not compelled labor.

class-collaboration.rationale: Libertarian socialists call wage labor wage slavery and seek to abolish the wage system and capitalism rather than make peace with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: libertarian socialists attack hierarchical institutions but do not generally call for destroying libraries and culture, which they regard as common heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Libertarian socialists support anti-colonial struggle but distrust state and nationalist fronts, so they are split.

workers-nation.rationale: Anarchism is internationalist and critical of nationalism and borders, and organizes workers across nations as a class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose patriarchy and have an anarcha-feminist strand, and they reject law imposing roles on anyone.

ban-interest.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject state coercion and law as such, so a legal ban on lending is contrary to their approach.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose hierarchy and the state's power to classify and coerce, and stand in solidarity with migrants against nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Kropotkin saw the state as an instrument of landlordism and capitalism; Chomsky stresses wealthy-class control while allowing it can be held accountable.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Social libertarian socialists oppose profit-driven extraction and green strands are strongly ecological; inferred from the critique of capitalism.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nationalism and borders and practice migrant solidarity, so demanding assimilation to a national culture runs against their core stance.

elite-replacement.rationale: Libertarian socialists reject nationalism and ethnic-nativist framings; inferred from their internationalism and migrant solidarity.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta and the social anarchist tradition reject parliament and voting as a route to freedom, so tinkering with seat allocation is not their goal.

national-mission.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose the state and nationalism and are internationalist and anti-militarist, so exporting a national government is rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarchism extends its critique of hierarchy to patriarchy, and anarcha-feminism is an established strand.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that government is a class instrument that corrupts those who rule and serves privilege against ordinary people.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State coercion over reproduction contradicts anarchist opposition to coercive hierarchy and defense of individual autonomy; inferred from those principles.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Libertarian socialists want abuses answered for but distrust state courts and aim to abolish the police; inferred, so support is modest.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian socialists seek to abolish the state altogether and see police and army as tools of exploitation and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose nationalism and every hierarchy of group over group, and defend free choice in personal life.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and treats all people as equals, but it rejects state law, so 'rights before the law' is only partly its framing.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: libertarian socialists are internationalists who hold revolution must spread and who criticised Marxist state socialism for degenerating.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from anarchist anti-nationalism and anti-colonialism, which reject claims of a people to a state over displaced populations.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: libertarian socialists reject both religious authority and state-made law, so they favour neither a common state code nor communal personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Libertarian socialists defend free thought and oppose state coercion in matters of belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: libertarian socialists oppose state prohibitions enforcing religious sentiment, though vegan and animal-liberation strands favour the aim.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred: libertarian socialists are anti-clerical and secular and oppose religious doctrine in schools, though they also reject state schooling itself.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bakunin's critique of Marxism held that a strong transitional state entrenches a new ruling class; libertarian socialists want the state abolished at once.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that only voluntary association is legitimate, though they reject the very idea of being governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; they see rivalry for world power as capitalist competition, and want producers as collaborators.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts the anti-authoritarian and internationalist principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pacifist strands accept it, but expropriation and sabotage are defended by others, and property is defined differently.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Chomsky's critique of intellectual elites and the anarchist suspicion of expert rule suggest agreement that claims of knowledge serve power, though adherents differ; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Libertarian socialists share the anarchist and council-communist view that cooperation and solidarity, not competition, are the basis of a good society.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Libertarian socialists distrust state power and would oppose banning parties, though they do not defend parliamentary parties as such; inferred from their anti-authoritarianism.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Libertarian socialists hold that wage labour and hierarchical authority make people unfree even when the boss does not interfere, which is why they call for self-management.

separated-powers.rationale: Libertarian socialists want power dispersed and federated from below, but council communists and anarchists reject state branches as the means; inferred and split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Libertarian socialism rejects vanguard parties, and council communists such as Pannekoek held that workers' councils must run their own struggle.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The family sides with workers and the exploited, but seeks to remove class by self-management rather than by laws ranking the poor first; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose both private and state ownership and favour tenant or community control, so a right to buy is not their demand; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Direct action and workers organising from below are core, and they distrust state limits on it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They locate poverty in capitalism and state power rather than numbers; inferred from the core critique.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Carried over from the anarchist and council-communist core, which is internationalist and rejects the cohesion-by-sameness claim; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: They favour direct democracy and delegates in councils; lottery is not a stated position, so inferred as split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: They are anti-authoritarian and oppose emergency state powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; they prefer community control of distribution over state ceilings; inferred as split.

party-controls-media.rationale: They reject state control and favour free, decentralised organisation from below, which excludes state or party control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Pannekoek and the anarchists reject state and party power, and favour workers militias over a party army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Anarchist-derived internationalism and critique of borders; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Council communists and anarchists hold that delegates live as workers do, as in the Paris Commune model; inferred from their opposition to a privileged political class.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Anarchist and council currents favour free association and reject binding discipline by a party or leadership, though federations expect mandated delegates; inferred from anti-authoritarian principles.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Libertarian socialists oppose supranational states and unions as centralised power, preferring federations from below; inferred from the anti-state core.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rejecting the state means rejecting a ruler commanding armed forces and choosing ministers; the family prefers armed people and no standing executive.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy and church authority alike, and favour free association from below over appointed bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy is rejected by anarchists and council communists as authority that is both statist and religious.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anti-war internationalists in this family, from Bakunin to Luxemburg, treat inter-imperialist war as a ruling-class affair and urge opposition to one own government; adherents split on tactics.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Libertarian socialists defend free expression and oppose state censorship as an instrument of authority; inferred from the anti-authoritarian core.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They reject presidents and permanent office; where officials exist they favour rotation and short mandates, so unlimited re-election is opposed; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Revocable, mandated delegates are a central principle of council democracy and direct democracy.

notes: The family is broad: individualist and market-socialist strands accept markets, democratic-socialist strands accept the state, and pacifist strands reject violence. Answers not stated in the four sources were carried over from the anarchist profile and downgraded in confidence.
